_meta.purpose: Real-course data for the RunTheTour Daily Challenge. Each course carries its real scorecard (per-hole par + yardage + name) joined to the DataGolf skill-fit weights (the `fit` block, copied from COURSEFIT / course_fit.json). `fit` keys: dist acc app sht scr bnk put clu.
_meta.tees: Championship / tournament tees, most recent setup.
_meta.provenance: Scorecards researched from PGA Tour media scorecards, BlueGolf course database, AllGolfHoles, course/championship sites. 12 courses fully verified hole-by-hole; East Lake (post-2024 redesign) and Sedgefield are structure-accurate (correct par, par-3/4/5 counts, finishing holes) with approximate per-hole yardages — flagged with verified:false for later refinement. 2026-07 expansion: 23 more courses added (majors, Open rota links courses, and iconic PGA Tour stops), researched via web search and cross-checked across multiple sources; individual hole yardages flagged verified:false where not confirmed against one authoritative scorecard. avg/cdiff Monte-Carlo-calibrated against the live daily-challenge engine so a flat OVR-80 build averages the researched real-world scoring average.

Augusta National.blurb: A crystalline test of nerve through blooming azaleas, where slope and water punish the slightest misstep.

signatureHoles.why: Amen Corner's perilous short par-3 over Rae's Creek — swirling wind, tiny green
Par-5 dogleg in Amen Corner; eagle chance but water guards the green
Par-5 over water where late eagles and bogeys decide the Masters

TPC Sawgrass.blurb: A Pete Dye stage of island-green terror and precisely scaled par-4s, where accuracy beats power.

signatureHoles.why: The island-green par-3 at 137 yards ringed by water — golf's most feared short hole
Reachable par-5 before 17 — an eagle look that sets up a daring finish
Brutal par-4 with water all down the left — a nervy closer

Pebble Beach Golf Links.blurb: Eight holes hug cliffs above the Pacific, where beauty and peril merge into America's greatest seaside test.

signatureHoles.why: The world's most photographed par-3, 106 yards downhill to a cliffside green
Cliff-carry approach over a chasm — one of golf's great second shots
Par-5 hugging the ocean the whole way left — an iconic finish

St Andrews Old Course.venue: The Old Course at St Andrews
St Andrews Old Course.blurb: Golf's cathedral — double greens, hidden pot bunkers and wind test patience across 600 years of links tradition.

signatureHoles.why: The Road Hole par-4 — Road Bunker and the wall behind make it maybe golf's hardest par-4
Long par-5 with Hell Bunker lurking — bold seconds flirt with disaster
Drivable home hole over the Swilcan Burn into the town — birdie or heartbreak

Oakmont.blurb: The brutest test in golf — Church Pews bunkers, glassy greens and choking rough demand flawless execution.

signatureHoles.why: The Church Pews — a vast bunker of grass ridges between 3 and 4
At ~289 yards, the longest par-3 in major-championship golf
Drivable par-4 dangling a birdie amid Oakmont's torture

TPC Scottsdale.blurb: Home of the raucous par-3 16th 'Coliseum' and a drivable 17th — desert risk-reward with a stadium roar.

signatureHoles.why: The stadium par-3 ringed by 20,000 fans — golf's loudest hole
Drivable par-4 at 332 yards — go for the green and ignite the crowd
Reachable par-5 setting up the famous finish

Bay Hill.blurb: Arnold Palmer's exacting parkland test, capped by a fearsome water-guarded 18th that has decided countless titles.

signatureHoles.why: Water-guarded par-4 closer in a natural amphitheater — Palmer's signature drama
C-shaped par-5 bending around water — reward for the brave
Reachable par-5 swinging momentum down the stretch

Harbour Town Golf Links.blurb: Pete Dye's tight, tree-lined precision test through the Lowcountry, closing under the iconic candy-striped lighthouse.

signatureHoles.why: Exposed par-4 along Calibogue Sound to the lighthouse — a windswept, iconic finish
Coastal par-3 fully exposed to the wind
Demanding short par-3 to a shallow Dye green

Quail Hollow Club.blurb: A muscular layout whose closing 'Green Mile' (16-17-18) is one of the Tour's most punishing finishes.

signatureHoles.why: Closing par-4 with a creek down the entire left — a brutal finish
Par-3 to a water-guarded green in the Green Mile
536-yard par-4 to open the Green Mile gauntlet

Muirfield Village.blurb: Jack Nicklaus's exacting masterpiece through tree corridors and over water, with one of the Tour's hardest closing holes.

signatureHoles.why: Brutish par-4 closer with a creek left — routinely the hardest hole at the Memorial
Par-3 over water to a perched green — classic Nicklaus risk
Short, strategic par-4 demanding a precise wedge

Valhalla.blurb: A dramatic Nicklaus championship venue of water and limestone, often decided on the par-5 18th before the clubhouse.

signatureHoles.why: Island-green par-4 ringed by water and limestone rock
Reachable par-5 to the clubhouse — every PGA Championship here decided on it
Long par-5 'Genuine Risk' tempting a go at the green

TPC River Highlands.blurb: A short, birdie-friendly track with a thrilling risk-reward finish around the lake — the 'Bermuda Triangle' of 15-17.

signatureHoles.why: Drivable 296-yard par-4 with water left — supreme risk-reward
Par-3 over the lake to a shallow green in the Bermuda Triangle
Tight par-4 around the water to set up the finish

Plantation Course at Kapalua.blurb: A vast, wind-and-elevation playground above the Pacific, ending with the Tour's longest hole — a plunging par-5 18th.

signatureHoles.why: The Tour's longest hole — a 677-yard downhill par-5 you can ride the trade winds down
A huge downwind par-4 that plays far shorter than its yardage
A 550-yard par-4 — only at Kapalua

East Lake Golf Club.blurb: Historic Atlanta championship venue, recently lengthened to par 71 with a water-bisected par-5 closer that crowns the season.

signatureHoles.why: Long par-5 closer bisected by water — the Tour Championship's deciding hole
Reachable par-5 to spark a late charge
Long, demanding par-3 to a guarded green

Glen Abbey.blurb: Jack Nicklaus's first solo design — an open front nine and a daring, water-laced 'valley' back nine, long home to the Canadian Open.

signatureHoles.why: Start of the famous 'valley holes' plunging toward Sixteen Mile Creek
Water-guarded par-4 closer where Tiger's 2000 bunker shot became legend
Par-5 in the valley tempting an aggressive second

Sedgefield Country Club.blurb: A classic 1926 Donald Ross design of subtle turtle-back greens and clever bunkering — finesse over power.

signatureHoles.why: Downhill par-4 closer off an elevated tee
Long, exacting par-3 — one of the course's stoutest holes
Reachable par-5 offering a late birdie before the finish

Pinehurst No. 2.blurb: Donald Ross's 1907 masterpiece, its severe turtleback greens shed anything but a perfectly judged approach, punishing misses into sandy waste areas and wiregrass.

signatureHoles.why: A brutal 588-yard par 5 that stretches the round's toughest demand for precision off the tee
The longest hole at a U.S. Open, a 617-yard par 5 that tests both power and patience
Pinehurst's turtleback greens are never more punishing than on this short, dangerous par 4

Royal Troon.blurb: A brutal out-and-back Ayrshire links where the terrifying, tiny par-3 8th, the Postage Stamp, sits inside a murderous stretch of railway, gorse, and coastal wind.

signatureHoles.why: The Postage Stamp, golf's smallest and most feared par 3, a mere 123 yards ringed by deep pot bunkers
The Railway hole runs tight along the Glasgow-Ayr line with gorse choking the fairway, one of the hardest holes in Open rotation
Craigend's closing par 4 has decided Open Championships, including Henrik Stenson's 2016 duel with Phil Mickelson

Carnoustie.blurb: 'Carnasty' — a merciless finishing stretch where the twisting Barry Burn crosses the fairway three times and has ended championship dreams, most infamously Jean van de Velde's.

signatureHoles.why: The Barry Burn crossing in front of the Home green produced Jean van de Velde's catastrophic 1999 meltdown that cost him the Claret Jug
Hogan's Alley, named for Ben Hogan's daring line over the burn in his lone 1953 Open win, remains high-risk, high-reward
The Island hole demands a drive threaded between two bends of the Barry Burn, one of the tightest tee shots in championship golf

Royal Portrush.blurb: The Open's dramatic return to Northern Ireland after 68 years, where wild dunes, Atlantic wind, and the terrifying drop of Calamity Corner test nerve at every turn.

signatureHoles.why: Calamity Corner, a par 3 played over a yawning chasm to a narrow green, one of golf's most feared and photographed holes
Rory McIlroy's opening tee shot went out of bounds here in 2019, leading to a quadruple-bogey in front of his home crowd
Babington's closing hole saw Shane Lowry seal a six-shot win in brutal wind and rain to become Ireland's Open champion

Turnberry.blurb: A dramatic clifftop links beneath the Turnberry lighthouse, where Ailsa Craig looms over the Firth of Clyde and the closing holes have broken hearts, most famously Tom Watson's at 59.

signatureHoles.why: Bruce's Castle plays from a rocky promontory past the iconic lighthouse, with Ailsa Craig on the horizon
Duel in the Sun, named for the legendary 1977 Nicklaus-Watson finish — in 2009, 59-year-old Watson's approach here forced the playoff he'd lose to Stewart Cink
Lang Whang, the course's other par 5, swung the pivotal 2009 playoff after Watson's double bogey

Riviera Country Club.blurb: A canyon-carved George Thomas masterpiece where a mid-green bunker and a drivable, dagger-thin par-4 tenth have humbled legends since Hogan turned it into his personal 'Alley.'

signatureHoles.why: A par 3 famous for the bunker built directly into the middle of the green, splitting the surface into four tricky quadrants
A tempting, drivable par 4 ringed by bunkers that Jack Nicklaus called one of the greatest short holes in championship golf
An uphill, semi-blind closer climbing the canyon wall to a green that has decided the Genesis Invitational

Torrey Pines South.blurb: A rugged, wind-whipped municipal test perched on La Jolla's sea cliffs, where the par-3 3rd stares down the Pacific and a brutal closing stretch has decided U.S. Opens.

signatureHoles.why: A cliffside par 3 with a postcard Pacific Ocean backdrop, one of the most beautiful and intimidating tee shots in golf
The par-5 closer guarded by 'Devlin's Billabong,' where Tiger Woods drained a clutch birdie to force the legendary 2008 U.S. Open playoff
A monster 621-yard par 5 anchoring the demanding closing stretch, a key battleground in the 2021 U.S. Open

Innisbrook Copperhead.blurb: Pine-lined and unusually hilly for Florida, Copperhead bares its fangs in the closing 'Snake Pit,' Moccasin, Rattler, and Copperhead, where Valspar titles are won or lost.

signatureHoles.why: Moccasin, a heavily water-guarded par 4 that opens the fearsome Snake Pit finishing stretch
The Rattler, a long, well-bunkered par 3 demanding a precise long-iron with the tournament on the line
Packard's Double Dogleg, a bending 590-yard par 5 widely called the course's true signature hole

Waialae Country Club.blurb: A Seth Raynor gem along Waialae Beach, its template greens demand precise ball-striking while trade winds and Diamond Head views punish any lapse in a birdie-friendly but exacting test.

signatureHoles.why: Alae, a stunning Redan-style par 3 hugging Waialae Beach, its raised green guarded by deep bunkers and shifting trade winds
Kilou Loa, the closing par 5 where Isao Aoki holed a wedge for eagle in 1983 to win his only PGA Tour title
Welo, a demanding par 4 that sets up the dramatic finish along the shoreline

Colonial Country Club.blurb: A tight, tree-lined shotmaker's gauntlet along the Trinity River, where Ben Hogan's ghost still haunts the notorious Horrible Horseshoe.

signatureHoles.why: The par-3 heart of the 'Horrible Horseshoe' — a 247-yard terror to an elevated green that has never been aced in tournament history
The hardest hole at Colonial, a dogleg-right par 4 with a river right and ditch left demanding a precise tee shot
The signature par 3 over water where Colonial's tournament crowd gathers thickest

Southern Hills.blurb: A Perry Maxwell design where tree-lined corridors and a snaking creek punish any drive that strays, capped by a par 4 that Hogan and Palmer both called one of America's greatest.

signatureHoles.why: Praised by Hogan and Palmer as one of America's greatest par 4s, a dogleg left with a blind tee shot and a creek by the green
A short, driveable, risk-reward par 4 where Justin Thomas drove the green in the 2022 PGA Championship playoff
The longest hole on the course and the only par 5 on the front nine, a stern 656-yard test

Firestone South.blurb: A tree-lined Akron gauntlet built for power and precision, anchored by the 667-yard 'Monster' 16th and a Tiger Woods proving ground for two decades.

signatureHoles.why: The Monster, a 667-yard par 5 named by Arnold Palmer after a costly 1960 triple bogey, one of the longest par 5s in tour golf
A tree-lined closer where Tiger Woods struck his legendary 2000 'Shot in the Dark' to seal an 11-shot rout
Long rated the course's hardest hole, a tight, tree-guarded dogleg that breaks many contenders' rounds

Winged Foot.blurb: A merciless Tillinghast gauntlet of pinched fairways, cavernous bunkers, and severely canted greens that earned Winged Foot its 'Massacre' reputation in 1974.

signatureHoles.why: Ben Hogan called this par 3 'a 3-iron into someone's bedroom window,' a three-lobed green ringed by canyon-deep bunkers
The green where Phil Mickelson's 2006 meltdown, driver into a hospitality tent, a tree, a bunker, cost him the U.S. Open
A brutal 633-yard par-5 dogleg that stretches even the field's longest hitters to their limit

Bethpage Black.blurb: A public-course gauntlet by A.W. Tillinghast, where the first-tee warning sign promises 'extremely difficult,' and brutal length, deep bunkers, and unrelenting rough punish every miscalculation.

signatureHoles.why: The par-5 signature hole, split by a massive Sahara-style bunker complex that turns a birdie chance into a heroic gamble
Converted from a par 5 into a brutish, dogleg-right 520-yard par 4 for major championships
The toughest hole in multiple U.S. Opens, its approach climbs 50 feet to a green so steep locals sled down it in winter

Whistling Straits.blurb: A wind-lashed links carved into Lake Michigan's bluffs, guarded by over a thousand bunkers and a shoreline that turns every round into a survival test.

signatureHoles.why: Pinched Nerve demands a white-knuckle tee shot over dunes with a 20-foot drop to sand or Lake Michigan itself
Dyeabolical is Pete Dye's diabolical finisher, where Dustin Johnson's 2010 bunker ruling cost him a shot at the PGA Championship title
Cliff Hanger hugs the Lake Michigan shoreline with a narrow green perched above the water

Shinnecock Hills.blurb: A founding pillar of American golf, Shinnecock's windswept Long Island linksland tests firm fescue and domed greens where 2004's near-disaster gave way to 2018's hard-earned redemption.

signatureHoles.why: The brutal Redan-style par 3 whose baked-out green nearly broke the championship in 2004, forever synonymous with USGA overreach
Just 159 yards yet so ferocious Lee Trevino dubbed it 'the shortest par 5 in golf'
An uphill, partially blind finisher playing home to the Stanford White clubhouse, one of championship golf's great closing stages

Kiawah Island Ocean.venue: The Ocean Course at Kiawah Island
Kiawah Island Ocean.blurb: Pete Dye strips away every tree and hides his traps in plain sight, leaving golfers exposed on wind-lashed dunes where the Atlantic decides who out-thinks it and who doesn't.

signatureHoles.why: A fully exposed island-style par 3 dubbed the tournament's torture chamber, where Phil Mickelson's tense bogey nearly cost him the 2021 PGA Championship
An ocean-hugging par-4 closer where the 1991 'War by the Shore' Ryder Cup was decided with the Atlantic bearing down the entire hole
A near-600-yard par 5 that forces a gamble over a natural dune intrusion, epitomizing Dye's risk-reward deception

Olympic Club.blurb: Cypress-shadowed and relentlessly canted, this par-70 has spent seventy years luring the game's greatest names into historic collapse on one deceptively short, cruelly sloped green after another.

signatureHoles.why: A short, savage par 4 whose tiny hillside green has decided three separate U.S. Opens and nearly a fourth in 2012
One of the longest par-4 openers in U.S. Open history, offering no chance to ease into the round
The longest hole in U.S. Open championship history at 670 yards, testing endurance as much as ball-striking

Baltusrol.blurb: A Tillinghast gauntlet of diagonal bunkers and blind doglegs that builds to two monstrous closing par 5s, where a mid-fairway desert called the Sahara and a long slog to 18 have broken and made major champions alike.

signatureHoles.why: The Famous Fourth, a par 3 over a lake so demanding Robert Trent Jones defended his redesign by acing it himself in front of skeptical members
A three-shot par 5 bisected by the massive sandy Sahara waste complex, demanding two precise strikes just for position
The closing par 5 where Jack Nicklaus struck his legendary 1-iron approach to set up the winning birdie in the 1967 U.S. Open

The Country Club.blurb: An 1890s puzzle box of blind crests, tilted greens, and puddingstone ledge threaded between New England stone walls, where the low, historic Elbow can undo a round as easily as any brute par 5.

signatureHoles.why: Elbow, the most historically loaded hole in American golf — Ouimet birdied it to force the 1913 playoff, and Justin Leonard's putt here sealed the 1999 Ryder Cup comeback
Reintroduced for the 2022 U.S. Open as a deliberate callback to Francis Ouimet's legendary 1913 win
The closing hole where Matt Fitzpatrick sealed his 2022 U.S. Open title with a clutch bunker shot to a few feet

Merion.blurb: Merion disarms with its brevity, then punishes every loose swing with claustrophobic fairways, wicker baskets offering no wind clue, and a merciless quarry-scarred finish where precision beats power every time.

signatureHoles.why: Site of Bobby Jones's 1930 Grand Slam-clinching victory, its green nearly encircled by 'Baffling Brook,' swallowing any wayward approach
A long downhill par 3 over rock and scrub in 'the Quarry,' where Shawn Stefani made the first U.S. Open hole-in-one at Merion in 2013
An uphill finisher over the old quarry where Ben Hogan's iconic 1-iron won the 1950 U.S. Open

Oakland Hills.blurb: Robert Trent Jones dressed Donald Ross's rolling Michigan farmland in menacing new bunkers and tightened fairways until even Hogan, its conqueror, branded it a monster that had to be beaten into submission.

signatureHoles.why: A sharp dogleg right bending around a pond to a green guarded by water, demanding a precise second shot over hazard
A long, exposed par 3 regarded as the course's best one-shotter, offering little margin for error into a well-defended green
One of Donald Ross's original prized holes, with a severely sloping fairway that leaves a blind approach if the tee shot misses right

TPC Southwind.blurb: A humid, tree-lined gauntlet of zoysia fairways and water-guarded greens where a scaled-down island green and a brutal 231-yard par 3 decide the first FedEx Cup Playoffs cut.

signatureHoles.why: A 165-yard par 3 to a tiny island green, often called a smaller cousin of TPC Sawgrass's famous 17th
A 231-yard par 3 guarded by water down the entire right side, routinely ranked among the toughest par 3s on Tour
A demanding 453-yard closing par 4 that has decided the FedEx St. Jude Championship in playoffs and dramatic finishes
